title: Zero Trust Architecture & Identity
description: Never trust, always verify: explore continuous identity verification, MFA, and least-privilege access.

questions.question: What is the core philosophical tenet of a 'Zero Trust' security architecture?
options: Never trust, always verify every request regardless of location
Trust all internal traffic originating from the corporate VPN
Disable all SSL/TLS encryption for internal microservices
Use single-factor passwords for internal enterprise tools

questions.question: What is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) designed to prevent?
options: Unauthorized account access resulting from compromised single passwords
High network latency during database queries
Buffer overflow in compiled C programs
Overheating of mobile phone batteries

questions.question: What does the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP) dictate?
options: Entities are granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their authorized tasks
Every developer account has root privileges to eliminate deployment roadblocks
Passwords must be kept under 6 characters to improve login speed
All data stores must be accessible by default without credentials

questions.question: What is 'Micro-segmentation' in network security?
options: Creating granular, secure zones in data centers and cloud deployments to isolate workloads and limit lateral movement
Splitting monolithic web servers into React micro-frontends
Compressing TCP packet payloads into smaller sub-byte headers
Rotating DNS names every 5 seconds across edge POPs

questions.question: In cryptographic systems, what distinguishes Asymmetric encryption from Symmetric encryption?
options: Asymmetric uses a key pair (public & private), symmetric uses a single shared key
Asymmetric encryption cannot be decrypted once encrypted
Symmetric encryption is only usable for audio files
Asymmetric algorithms do not require mathematical operations
